meta.title: Service Delivery Source Catalog
meta.description: Curated high-authority sources for measuring services, products, discharges, prescriptions, facility service capabilities, and payment/utilization patterns beyond the current live MedTech workbook sheets.
meta.inclusion_rule: Include sources with an official steward, public documentation, explicit unit of observation, repeatable release cadence, and direct relevance to services provided or ordered.
limitations: This catalog is a source-selection layer, not a merged utilization file.
Most rows are Medicare public-use files and therefore do not represent Medicare Advantage, Medicaid, commercial insurance, uninsured care, or full clinical demand.
Operational use requires source-specific suppression rules, denominator alignment, geography checks, service-code interpretation, and release-year reconciliation.

sources.source_name: CMS Provider Summary by Type of Service
sources.unit_of_observation: Dataset family spanning provider, geography, service, facility, product, prescription, and payment summaries
sources.measurement_focus: Use, payments, procedures, services, prescription drugs, inpatient hospitals, outpatient hospitals, long-term care hospitals, inpatient rehabilitation facilities, skilled nursing facilities, home health agencies, hospices, physicians, suppliers, and Part D prescribers.
sources.join_keys: NPI; CCN; HCPCS; DRG; APC; geography; drug name; provider type depending on component dataset
sources.coverage: Original Medicare fee-for-service and Part D public-use products; component years vary
sources.why_it_matters: It is the strongest public launch point for expanding from physician service rows into institutional, post-acute, DME, and prescription service output.
sources.principal_caveat: It is a family of datasets, not one normalized table; each component has its own payer scope, suppression rules, unit, and release cadence.

sources.source_name: CMS Medicare Inpatient Hospitals — by Provider and Service
sources.measurement_focus: Inpatient discharges, payments, and hospital charges by provider and Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group.
sources.coverage: Original Medicare fee-for-service Part A IPPS hospitals; latest public-use year available from CMS
sources.why_it_matters: Adds institutional service-line volume and payment signals that physician HCPCS rows cannot see.
sources.principal_caveat: Limited to IPPS Medicare fee-for-service discharges and suppresses low-volume cells; it is not an all-payer inpatient service census.

sources.source_name: CMS Medicare Outpatient Hospitals — by Provider and Service
sources.unit_of_observation: OPPS hospital × ambulatory payment classification or HCPCS service
sources.measurement_focus: Outpatient service use, payments, submitted charges, and estimated hospital-specific charges by provider and service.
sources.join_keys: CCN; APC; HCPCS; hospital geography; year
sources.coverage: Original Medicare fee-for-service Part B OPPS hospitals; component years vary
sources.why_it_matters: Adds hospital outpatient procedures and diagnostics to the service-output view, including services not visible as office-based clinician rows.
sources.principal_caveat: OPPS scope and payment-policy exclusions must be checked before Maryland or cross-state comparison.

sources.source_name: CMS Medicare Part D Prescribers — by Provider and Drug
sources.measurement_focus: Prescription fills and drug costs for Medicare Part D beneficiaries by provider and drug.
sources.join_keys: NPI; drug brand name; drug generic name; geography; year
sources.coverage: Medicare Part D public-use data; latest public-use year available from CMS
sources.why_it_matters: Connects clinical service patterns to medication use and prescribing intensity, which are major delivered-service outputs for many fields.
sources.principal_caveat: Part D enrollment differs from fee-for-service Part B populations and the file does not represent all prescriptions or clinical appropriateness.

sources.source_name: CMS Medicare Durable Medical Equipment, Devices & Supplies — by Referring Provider and Service
sources.unit_of_observation: Referring provider NPI × HCPCS service × supplier rental indicator
sources.measurement_focus: DMEPOS usage, payments, and submitted charges for products and services ordered by clinicians.
sources.join_keys: Referring NPI; HCPCS; rental indicator; geography; year
sources.coverage: Original Medicare fee-for-service Part B DMEPOS non-institutional claim line items
sources.why_it_matters: Captures ordered medical equipment, devices, prosthetics, orthotics, and supplies that are often invisible in clinician visit counts.
sources.principal_caveat: Referring-provider rows are not the same as supplier capacity or patient access, and suppressed low-volume cells affect completeness.

sources.source_name: CMS Provider of Services File — Clinical Laboratories
sources.measurement_focus: Clinical laboratory demographics, certification characteristics, and types of testing services provided.
sources.join_keys: CMS Certification Number; CLIA-related provider attributes; address; certification status
sources.coverage: CMS Provider Certification process; quarterly public-use releases
sources.why_it_matters: Adds a facility-capability lens for testing services, useful where service availability depends on certified lab infrastructure rather than only clinician headcount.
sources.principal_caveat: Certification and listed testing capabilities do not directly measure test volume, turnaround time, payer access, or appointment availability.
